learningObjective: Identify the design motivations behind MetaSchedule / Ansor's approach to schedule search.
stem: The MetaSchedule / Ansor design line replaced hand-written schedule templates with an automatic pipeline. Which of the following are TRUE about the design motivations of that line? (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Manual per-operator templates are labor-intensive and do not generalize across new operator variants (e.g., new attention patterns, fused kernels), motivating an automatic sketch-generation stage.

A learned cost model is more predictive of measured runtime than a purely analytical model built on op counts and shape features alone, especially for GPU kernels where spills and bank conflicts matter.

The search space must be broken into a small number of algorithmic 'sketches' followed by numerical parameter annotation, so evolutionary search operates in a well-structured space rather than an unconstrained sequence of schedule primitives.
The system should replace real-hardware measurement with pure static analysis to eliminate measurement noise.
MetaSchedule sacrifices tuning quality for compile time; on any workload, a compiler with a manual template achieves better final kernels than MetaSchedule.

explanation: The Ansor / MetaSchedule design is motivated by three points: (A) hand-written templates are unsustainable as operators proliferate; (B) analytical cost models are inaccurate on modern GPUs — learned models trained on measured runtimes are more predictive; (C) the search proceeds in two phases (sketch generation for algorithmic structure, then annotation of numerical parameters) so evolutionary search operates over a well-typed space. D is directly contrary to Ansor's design — the authors explicitly retain real-hardware measurement while using the cost model for pruning. E overgeneralizes empirical results; MetaSchedule often matches or exceeds handwritten templates.

optionExplanations.B: Correct: learned cost model is more predictive on real hardware.
optionExplanations.C: Correct: sketch + annotation is the core structural design.
optionExplanations.D: Wrong: measurement is retained; cost model prunes candidates but real hardware ranks finalists.
optionExplanations.E: Wrong: empirical results show MetaSchedule often matches / beats hand-tuned templates.

assumptions: The comparison is made under equivalent tuning budgets.
nonImplications: Does not imply MetaSchedule eliminates all human input — sketch primitives and cost-model features are still designed.
Does not imply MetaSchedule is universally better; on some heavily-optimized templated cases, hand tuning can still win.

distractorRationales.D: Contradicts Ansor's explicit design choice to keep measurement.
